STORY 14.9 SEED LEVER — a byte-for-byte copy of comfyui_shot_recompose_qwen_api.json with sampler.seed 0 -> 20260830, and nothing else. It exists because the seed is NOT a code parameter: build_single_pass writes only plate/card/positive, and recompose_shot's `salt` is a ComfyUI upload filename that never reaches the sampler. Story 14.9's arms B and C SHARE THIS ONE FILE, so the only difference between them is the _DEPTH_PHRASE['near'] substitution; a per-arm seed would confound the prompt edit with a reroll. NOT a shipped default: no Settings field points here, so the style-contract sweep in tests/test_workflow_definitions.py does not classify it. Original note follows.

SHOT RECOMPOSE (Qwen-Image-Edit-2511) — Epic 10 '확정 방향'. Inputs are the CLEAN PLATE (image1) and the character CARDS (image2/image3), plus a natural-language placement instruction. The model decides where and at what size the character stands; no ffmpeg overlay, no ground_y arithmetic, no ControlNet silhouette lock. This replaces the composite-then-refine family that Jay rejected on 2026-08-09 (IC-Light relight / masked low-denoise fusion / ControlNet+IPAdapter on a composite still) — all three took an already-overlaid image as input, so placement stayed a code constant and characters kept floating on plates with no floor. Wiring is adapted from comfyui_qwen_pose_edit_api.json (Story 8.20), which is a working 2511 graph on this box; the difference is the inputs and that no rembg cutout is taken — the output is a full frame, not a sprite. Apache-2.0 weights, Q4_K_M 12GB. Injection points: 'plate'.image, 'card_a'.image, 'card_b'.image, 'positive'.prompt, 'sampler'.seed/steps/cfg/denoise.  VERIFIED 2026-08-09: 43-plate sweep (every approved location plate, one card, one fixed instruction) produced a usable frame for all 43 with zero composition failures; 1-character shots correct 4/4 on the run's own slate; 2-character shots correct via sequential insertion. Known residue: a circular bright patch appears under the figure on roughly half of plates whose own lighting vocabulary includes glowing floor elements — four prompt phrasings failed to remove it and an explicit 'do not add any circle' made it stronger (gotcha_negative-prompt-overstuffing again). Not fixed by prompting; judged in motion before spending more on it.

_meta.title: Qwen-Image-Edit-2511 Q4_K_M — Apache-2.0, ~12GB. 8.20's OOM figure was a different build and a different job.

fp8 text encoder (8.7GB) — REQUIRED, not a size choice. Qwen-Image-Edit needs the Qwen2.5-VL VISION tower to read image1/image2; the Q4 GGUF text encoder ships text-only and its vision weights live in a separate mmproj file. Loading it logged 'Can't find mmproj file ... Qwen-Image-Edit will be broken', dropped every visual.* weight, and every prompt died on 'mat1 and mat2 shapes cannot be multiplied (720x1280 and 3840x1280)'. The memory cost is paid with --lowvram (10.1e removed --disable-smart-memory: it re-read all 22.6 GB per pass, 385-677 s/pass vs 108 without it).
CLEAN background plate — the shot's own image, with NO card overlaid. This is the scene the character is placed into.
Character card 1 — identity reference. Its pixels are not pasted anywhere.
Character card 2 — omitted from the prompt encoder when a shot has one character.
The plate is the canvas: encoding it fixes the output size to the plate and keeps the room. Background is a reused fixed source by policy and must survive.

image1=plate, image2/3=cards. The prompt is the PLACEMENT INSTRUCTION — size, position, pose, contact with the floor — which is what the LLM already decides as position/depth/pose and which the old path flattened into fixed fractions.
Deliberately empty — gotcha_negative-prompt-overstuffing: adding a clause per defect wrecked renders twice.
4 steps / cfg 1.0 — the Lightning LoRA's operating point. denoise stays 1.0: the frame is generated from the plate latent, not retouched.
Full recomposed frame — NOT a cutout. 8.20 took a rembg cutout here because it was making a sprite; this path outputs the finished shot image.
Lightning 4-step LoRA (already on disk from 8.20). Cuts sampling to 4 steps; loading, not sampling, is the bottleneck here, but it keeps each probe cheap.
